tools.upiPractice.title: UPI practice
tools.upiPractice.pretend: Pretend screens. No real payment happens here.
tools.upiPractice.moneyOut: Where the money goes: {{amount}} out of your account.
tools.upiPractice.moneyIn: Where the money goes: {{amount}} into your account, with nothing for you to do.
tools.upiPractice.score: You kept your money safe on {{correct}} of {{total}} screens.
tools.upiPractice.rule: One rule covers every screen you just saw.
tools.upiPractice.rule.pin: A UPI PIN only ever sends money. You never need it to receive.
tools.upiPractice.rule.receive: Money sent to you simply arrives. No PIN, no QR scan, no approval.
tools.upiPractice.rule.otp: An OTP is a key to your account. No bank, shop or helpline will ask you to read it out.
tools.upiPractice.canteen.screen: You ate lunch and scanned the canteen's QR code yourself. The screen asks for your UPI PIN to pay {{amount}}.
tools.upiPractice.canteen.decline: Cancel, a PIN is never safe
tools.upiPractice.canteen.why: You chose to pay, you checked the name and the amount, and a PIN is how money is sent. This is the normal use.
tools.upiPractice.refund.screen: A message says your {{amount}} refund is ready: "Approve this request and enter your PIN to receive it."
tools.upiPractice.refund.why: This is a collect request. Approving it with your PIN sends {{amount}} to the stranger. A real refund arrives by itself.
tools.upiPractice.friend.screen: Asha is paying back the {{amount}} she borrowed. A pop-up from an unknown number says "enter your PIN to accept".
tools.upiPractice.friend.decline: Do nothing and wait for the credit message
tools.upiPractice.friend.why: Money sent to you needs nothing from you. The bank's credit message is the proof; a PIN prompt here is someone else's request.
tools.upiPractice.prizeQr.screen: "You have won {{amount}}! Scan this QR code and enter your PIN to collect your prize."
tools.upiPractice.prizeQr.decline: Ignore it and block the number
tools.upiPractice.prizeQr.why: Scanning a QR code and entering a PIN is how you pay. Nobody receives money that way, so the {{amount}} would leave your account.
tools.upiPractice.otpCall.screen: The caller says a payment of {{amount}} is leaving your account and asks you to read out the OTP "to cancel it".
tools.upiPractice.otpCall.decline: Hang up and call the number on my passbook
tools.upiPractice.otpCall.why: The OTP is what approves the payment. Reading it out is what makes the {{amount}} leave. Hang up and call the bank's official number yourself.
